Sober Agentic Infrastructure (Dallas, TX; remote-friendly) is hiring a contract kernel / formal-methods engineer.

We build VAREK, a compiled policy language and enforcement runtime that verifies an autonomous AI agent's proposed action before it executes. A policy compiles to a proof obligation discharged by an SMT decision procedure, which returns a three-way verdict: SATISFIED, UNSATISFIED, or UNKNOWN. Only SATISFIED actions reach the kernel; enforcement is at the syscall boundary via seccomp-BPF and seccomp user-notify. The runtime is SHIPPED (v1.9.2).

The work sits at two layers:

  • Kernel / syscall enforcement: seccomp-BPF allowlist design, seccomp user-notify supervision, syscall-boundary interception, and the ABI-level edge cases that come with it.
  • Formal methods: sharpening the compilation from policy to proof obligation, the soundness argument behind the three-way verdict, and compositional verification over multi-step action graphs.

Background that fits: Linux kernel or systems security (seccomp, BPF, syscall internals), and/or formal verification and proof engineering (proof assistants, SMT-backed reasoning, program semantics). You do not need both in equal measure; the pairing is the point.

Structure: contract, remote, scoped engagement to start, with room to grow as the first seed dollar funds a full technical hire. The technology is patent-pending (three provisional filings). I am the founder and will be your technical counterpart on the work; physician by training, now building this full time.

If this is interesting, reach me at kenneth.douglas@soberagents.ai with a sentence or two on which layer you gravitate toward and anything relevant you have shipped or proven.
